patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Linear and Trello share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Linear only if your buying job matches “Modern issue tracker for product/engineering teams — Free limited; Basic from ~$8/user/mo ” rather than Trello's shape. Choose Trello only if your buying job matches “Lightweight Kanban boards (Atlassian) — Free; Standard from $5/user/mo annual.” rather than Linear's shape. Workflow advantage: Linear leans work-management; Trello leans team-collaboration-work. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Linear and Trello share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Linear is Modern issue tracker for product/engineering teams — Free limited; Basic from ~$8/user/mo annual.; Trello is Lightweight Kanban boards (Atlassian) — Free; Standard from $5/user/mo annual..
- Company-size focus: Linear (startup, small-business, mid-market) vs Trello (micro, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Linear-leaning work-management vs Trello-leaning team-collaboration-work.
- Researched limits: Linear — Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS; Trello — Limited planning depth vs Work OS.

Limitations — Linear: Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS; Leaner automation than Jira Enterprise; Trello: Limited planning depth vs Work OS; Premium needed for richer views.

Poor-fit cases: Linear is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not for company-wide marketing/ops Work OS · Trello is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Limited planning depth vs Work OS · Avoid Linear if you actually need Trello's motion (Lightweight Kanban boards (Atlassian) — Free; Standard from $5/user/mo annual.)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
